sessionStart.prompt: This repository may use the knowledge-folder convention (.arc42, .domain, .tech, .design, .backlog). Treat those folders as task-scoped context, not baseline context: load only the chapters the current task needs, never the whole folder by default. Every file and every addressable chapter in them carries a fenced `meta` block; when you create or edit one, write that block in the same change. Files under any _meta/ folder are generated - never hand-edit them, regenerate them instead. Route edits to these folders through the matching skill: .arc42 chapter content -> orch-arc42-content (but decision records, technical debt records, and blueprints go to orch-adr, orch-tdr, orch-blueprint, or orch-architecture); .domain -> orch-domain; .tech -> orch-tech; .design -> orch-design; .backlog -> orch-backlog. When the task is bidirectional - writing a chapter from something already implemented, or turning an agreed chapter into implementation work - route through capture-<kind> or build-<kind> instead, where <kind> is one of aggregate, domain-service, feature, term, bounded-context, building-block, deployment, or design-component; capture reads code and unit tests and routes its write through the orchestration above, build emits a change brief and stops without touching source or test trees. An aggregate is captured and built whole - the root plus the entities, value objects, and enums it owns and the domain events it raises - so there is no separate entity, value-object, or domain-event skill; a domain service keeps its own pair and owns the events it raises itself. A repository may provide its own repo-native skills under .github/skills/, and those take precedence for the categories they cover.
